plain_text: Monday Nite Footballers Predictions By Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly Predicting Since 1970 Hank Stram, Enlarging Our Territory Hank Stram was the first head coach of the Kansas City Chiefs. Only those of us over 50 will remember the days when Kansas City was part of the old American Football League. This was the early sixties, when the predominant National Football League touted franchises. . . like the Chicago Bears, San Francisco Forty-Niners, and the Washington Redskins. And Hank Stram and others had the task of competing with and enlarging the territory of the fragile but willing League. And enlarge they did. And Hank Stram, under the guidance of Lamar Hunt, brought Kansas City up from nowhere into the big leagues. Before merging, the AFL actually had to outbid and outwit the more formidable NFL. More important, they also had to outplay them, as well. And that’s where Hank Stram came in. With smaller, lesser-known players, Hank had to be an innovator. With a small, frail quarterback like Len Dawson, Stram implemented a “moving pocket”. That allowed the bigger, faster offensive linemen to outmaneuver the slower, meaner defensive linemen. And that would lead to a more fan-friendly game. While Hank was a master at coaching, he knew how to motivate the newly-found, small-college athletes. Especially the young athletes from Grambling, Southern, and Texas Southern. And it is here where he will be most remembered by folks of color. Never was there any kind of racial uprising or unfair play on any of Stram’s teams. He just didn’t tolerate it and he made everybody feel included. More important, he treated them fairly at the pocketbook level, as well. Many came poor and left well-paid, especially in their later years. In conclusion, Hank Stram was more than innovation to this new-f league. He was more than a coach, who coined phrases like “matriculating down the field”. Since Stram was in charge, we have not been near a Super Bowl. But he was right up there with Branch Rickey, who cleared the path for Jackie Robinson to play major league baseball. With the same level of commitment, Stram cleared the “economic path” for these young unheard-of athletes, to make a lot of money. Simple as that. He did enlarge our territory. Thanks, Hank.

Monday Niters Chatter, Conversation and Commentary Super Bowl 42, No Competition February is Black History Month. It’s also the month when 22 states will decide its presidential preference. Of lesser importance, it is also the birthday month of our nation’s founding president, George Washington. And for lovers, the month houses Valentine’s Day. But all this will not hold a candle to Super Bowl 42, featuring the undefeated-going-perfect New England Patriots against the never-quitting New York Giants. But, the game is only a small part. People will be talking about the million-dollar commercials. Already, one sponsor has set aside 16 million to be first in the commercial queue. Add to that the multi-million dollar half-time show (people are still talking about the Janet Jackson fiasco). And most of all, folks are lining the pockets of the Las Vegas casinos. . . rying to pick a for-sure winner. Right now, New England has the edge and everybody is talking about the Brady to Toomer nexus. But what about Little, less-famous brother Eli Manning. Now, that is the real story of this Super Bowl. For nearly ten years, everybody has been talking about Big Brother, Priceless Peyton. And for the record, he was supposed to lead the Colts into Phoenix. Instead, it was Eli who is going to the Big Ball. There is hope for us all. Which brings me to my real message about the Monday Nite Footballers Group. As we all elderize, we can go back to Super Bowl One and Four and any other. We saw Doug Williams set a Super Bowl record for most touchdowns scored in a Super Bowl. We’ve even witnessed running backs like Terrell Davis gallop from one end of the stadium to the other. We’ve known Kansas Citians, like Ralph Brown, who always went to the Super Bowl. And finally, we remembered way back when the Chiefs were in the Super Bowl. I believe it was against Minnesota. I believe it was Otis Taylor who starred that day. He made a little kick going into the end zone. Pardon us for not being sure about all the details. . . for it has been 39 years since the Chiefs were there. Hint. Hint. Do you hear us, Peterson and Edwards?

Kerry Washington, The Golden Rule And The 9-2 Chiefs Long before Kerry Washington became “a Thursday night must-see”, she starred along side Jamie Foxx in the 2004 major flick, “Ray”. In fact, she played Ray Charles’ wife and stood firm and steady, all through Ray Charles’ ups and downs and yes, even a nasty heroin addiction. We all knew then that Kerry would rise to the top, especially since she possesses the ability to use “all of her” in her acting craft. Eyes. Nose, Forehead. Eyebrows.Facial creases. This woman exudes totality and entirety. Everything about her makes the scene advance. When acting, Kerry rules. Speaking of rules, let’s talk a minute about the Golden Rule. While many think this is a biblical expression, it really came along, long before Christianity. It simply says “do unto others as you would have them do unto you”. Well, the Chiefs will have a chance to do just that against Denver this Sunday. Beaten badly in the “mile-high” city two weeks ago, the Broncos will come riding into Arrowhead, after a horse-whipping from the New England Patriots last Sunday. Yes, Denver jumped out to a 24-0 lead, only to fall to the “totally magic arm” of Tom Brady. Eventually, the Patriots prevailed with a record-breaking comeback, in the second half. The first half, all Denver. The second half, it was all New England. That brings us to the Chiefs and Denver. Both teams are vying for the AFC West and a guarantee of home-field advantage in the playoffs. And really, it’s much more. Kansas City has to prove that it can “hang” with the best teams, a second time. Against San Diego, the offense finally showed up and the defense went to sleep. Jamaal Charles ran like crazy, while Hali and Houston fell to injuries. And more important, “AWOL Alex” Smith threw for nearly 300 yards. Where in the hell have you been, Alex? Bottom line, the Chiefs will need everything and everybody to beat Denver, especially since Denver was” totally embarrassed” before God and country. Like Kerry Washington, the Chiefs will need to express themselves, just like Smith finally did. Otherwise, the Kansas City fans will consider it a “scandal” and turn the tv off, reminding us of the days-gone-by when they lost all the time. Ahhhh. An idea. Let’s call in Olivia Pope and see if she can fix this scandal or do something to make it right. No, not just yet. Let’s give the Chiefs one more chance, to put together a complete game, where the offense moves the ball and the defense rides the bucking Broncos. Faith. Faith. Faith. Just a little more faith. And a lot of the Golden Rule. Dr. Charles Allen: It’s a “must-win”. Chiefs by 10. Mrs. Mila Lewis Banks: Chiefs lost their best tacklers. Denver by 7. Paul Booker: K.C’s defense is no longer enthusiastic. Denver by 14 Carl Clark: Alex Smith has been exposed. Denver by 7. Bubba Cleaver: These are troubling times in the kingdom. Denver by 10. Ike Gardner: Defense is nonexistent without Hali and Houston. Denver by 20. Lloyd Greenfield: It’ll be a struggle, but K.C. will prevail. Chiefs by 3. Ollie Hubbard: Do unto others as they HAVE done unto you. Chiefs by 6. Jim Nunnelly: K.C. will employ Kerry-Washington-like totality. Chiefs by 6. Ed West: KC has too many defensive injuries. Denver by 10.

Monday Niters By Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly Well, we all know that the Chiefs are still losing. But, so is Oakland, the Chiefs’ next Arrowhead opponent. And, we all know about the 40 year rivalry between the two teams. And we also know that, at one time, these AFC stalwarts were competitive and even Super Bowl entrants. But, like a lot of things, each of these two historical giants have fallen on “hard times”. Neither is expected to do much at all, in 2008. Like last year and the year before that. In fact, these conference siblings are in a shaky state of re-building i.e. they will lose every game they play. Thus, the game out at Arrowhead will be “a battle of the behinders”. To mark such a sad occasion, I have changed the names of the teams, to reflect how even they are. . . in their likelihood to lose. From now on, these two teams are called the Kansas City Raiders and the Oakland Chiefs. That’s because they are both losers and they will continue doing “hard times of 2008”. Enough said. Allow me tell you a little about each one of the Monday Nite Footballers Group. . . one by one. . . with their predictions for Sunday. DR. CHARLES ALLEN (Kansas City) -- A dentist by profession. . . known for his painless procedures and his professional office staff. . a Kappa by fraternity.... an extraordinary grandfather. . . believes Kansas City will win by touchdown because the Chiefs will play better at home. PAUL BOOKER..(Oakland). . . retired educator...was a specialist in assisting needy students...hails from the Bootheel. . . watches ESPN everyday...good with figures...self-appointed liquor inspector...fantastic grandfather. . . believes Oakland will win by 10 because of the pitiful Chiefs’ pitiful offensive line. CARL CLARK (Kansas City). . . retired journeyman at Colgate...car enthusiast. world traveler...socially aware and respected. . . effective grandfather....daily visitor to 69th and Prospect. . . believes Kansas City will win by a touchdown, even though neither team is worthy of winning. BUBBA CLEAVER.(Kansas City). . . nationally-acclaimed elected official and minister. . . former Mayor and now United States Congressman. . .studious and thoughtful to a fault.. . . can remember thousands of people and their exact conversations. . . a proud grandfather. . . believes Kansas City will win by 10 because the Oakland Raiders don’t “raid” any more. IKE GARDNER..(Oakland). . . fearless pragmatist. . . attends St. James and sits near the back on the aisle. . .a steadfast grandfather. . . cantankerous as hell. . . has seats on the 50 yard line at Arrowhead. . . was a key player in the early days of desegregation of schools. . .believes Kansas City by 3 because there is no chance for Oakland to win. LLOYD GREENFIELD (Kansas City). . . a retired firefighter turned real estate enthusiast. . . owns hundreds of model cars...has a motorcycle. . . has starred in many theatrical events. . . clear-headed and respected. . . stays in contact with his old high school class..believes the Chiefs will win by 3 but it will be on a “wing and a prayer”. OLLIE HUBBARD (Oakland). . . Loves and is married to Lincoln university. . . been known to lie about everything. . . knows everybody in Kansas City...formerly a vice principal, now retired....loves to prepare food for his friends so that he can eat the most.....a remarkable grandfather....thinks the Kansas City-Oakland game will be a toss-up but Chiefs could win by 14. JIM NUNNELLY..(Kansas City). . .has consulted with over 200 organizations nationwide....instrumental in building anddeveloping the Rodgers Health Center. . . .a relentless advocate for teenagers. . . a complete grandfather.......works at Jackson County. . . believes the Chiefs and the Raiders are the two worst teams in the NFL but come Sunday, the Chiefs will deploy a “Midwest Coast Defense” and win by 3. ED WEST....(Kansas City). . . a gadgetician. . . can construct or repair any computer...has a huge big screen tv. . .a substitute teacher in Raytown....was All-America at Pittsburg State. . .devout member of St. James. . . an encouraging grandfather...believes Kansas City will win by a touchdown because he “just a Raider-hater”

Flip Wilson, Old Sayings And The 11-4 Chiefs You all remember Flip Wilson. He had his own television show, way back in the sixties. In fact, he was one of the first African American comedians to have a major white following. Most people will remember him as “Geraldine”, a cross-dressed character he created for the show. Everyone like ol’ Flip and he sure did a lot to reduce racial tensions, nationwide. Everyone waited for and watched Flip Wilson do his thing on Sunday evenings. Speaking of doing things, the Chiefs failed to win, out at Arrowhead this last Sunday. But don’t fret too much because they will be still be playing after they play Sunday against the Chargers.. That simply means they have played well enough and won enough games to “qualify” for the Super Bowl chase. However, two things. They have to win to stay in the mix. And secondly, they have to play on the road. Now, remember when the Chiefs won the Super Bowl after the 1969 season, they were in the same position. They were a wild card entry, which means they can pursue the Super Bowl….but they have to play on the road. If you want to know more about the only Super Bowl the Chiefs have played in, just ask Ike Gardner. He is still mad because the Chiefs have never regained the respect they once had, when they won the “big game” against the Joe Kapp and the Minnesota Vikings. Speaking of Ike and his cantankerous ways, I owe him somewhat of an apology. You will remember last week, I talked about how Ike had consistently beat up on the Chiefs. In spite of them winning eleven games this year, he still insists they are a mediocre team at best. Truthfully, they are much more than they were last year. But last Sunday against Indianapolis , they stunk. I mean less than mediocre. After the first series touchdown, the Chiefs went downhill, the rest of the game. Thatcaused national commentators to talk badly about the Chiefs, as well. They say that the Chiefs can’t win against teams with winning tradition and records. That sounds like what Ike has been saying. Really, I don’t mind what Ike says. I just don’t like the way he says it. There’s no love or loyalty in his cantankerous comments. He sounds so disloyal. Unlike other Monday Niters like Dr. Allen, Paul Booker, Carl Clark, Bubba Cleaver, Lloyd Greenfield, Ollie Hubbard and Ed West, Ike just blatantly “tells it like it is”. And readers everywhere just are appalled at his non-support of the home team. But another old saying may apply. “It is what it is”. The Chiefs are shaky some days. But some days, they show great promise, especially among players like Derrick Johnson and Jamaal Charles and even Tamba Hali. Another old saying is that “you can’t make a silk purse out of a pig’s ear”. That means you have to accept what the Chiefs are and they are a good team…but not a great team like New England or Denver or New Orleans or even Seattle. Ike would say the Chiefs will not make it through the first round in the playoffs. But they made it this far and they will be trying to advance. And they will be on tv, when most teams will be watching. Getting back to tv, we started out talking about Flip Wilson having his own tv show, way back when. And like all of our favorite shows, something is said that sticks with us all of our life. And it just may well wrap up this conversation about the Chiefs. Old Flip used to say somewhere during every telecast. What You See Is What You Get” And that my friends describes our Kansas City Chiefs. So Ike needs to call on Flip to help him state his disdain, more appropriately.

Monday Nite Footballers Predictions By Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly Predicting Since 1970 Charles Allen (9) Chiefs by 3 Chiefs will take a bite out of Bengals Paul Booker (5) Cincinnati by 14 Chiefs not ready for the big show! Bubba Cleaver (8) Lloyd Greenfield (9) Chiefs by 3 All is well that ends well Kansas City Chiefs vs. Cincinatti Bengals 12:00 p.m. KCTV 5 “Forks In The Road” Obviously, this game is it! The Chiefs have come to the fork in the road…either they win or we will all turn our attention and support to Tony Dungy (Indianapolis) and Marvin Lewis (Cincinnati). But if Detroit should happen to beat Pittsburg and Denver wipes out San Diego and the Chiefs beat up on Cincinnati…. then, the Chiefs will make the playoffs. Folks, it is that simple. And complicating matters is the hovering speculation that Vermeil will retire…one way or the other. Clearly, Vermeil is at the fork in the road, too. Win and stay in! Lose and sign up for Medicare! Folks, it is that simple. And we, Monday Niters, are facing another kind fork in the road. Monday Night Football, as we know it, is over. ABC will no longer broadcast the perennial ratings-winner. In fact, we all said our goodbyes to Al Michaels and John Madden and reminisced about all the history-making plays witnessed on Monday night television, everywhere. In 1970, we were all younger, quicker, and immature. Now we are older, slower and fall asleep, with no warning. It takes us longer to do EVERYTHING, including selecting our teams. Some of us even have to ask “who’s playing”. The fork in the road for us is that we are just getting old and things are changing, with or without our support. But some things will never change….Ike, Ollie and that Booker will always be haters of the Chiefs. Cleaver, Carl, and Ed West will go with the wind. And faithful, fine people like Lloyd Greenfield and imminent Dr. Allen, will always support the Chiefs, just like on New Year’s Day against North Division champions, Cincinnati. We know the Chiefs will win by at least ten and Vermeil stays in. We never have been at that fork in the road! Like each of you, we will have to switch the channel over to ESPN and carry on as usual. Booker, Ollie and Ike will continue to hate the Chiefs. And Ed, Carl and Cleaver will switch up, every now and then. And Dr. Charles Allen, Lloyd Greenfield and I will always support the Chiefs. Wisely, we don’t have to face a fork in the road. We know the way, just like we have always done. And just for the record, we will be looking for the Chiefs to win on New Year’s Day, out at Arrowhead. Chiefs by 10 and Vermeil will be back, again! Super Bowl XLIII: Arm Vs. Hammer Amid all the opulent commercials, the teams on the field were not expected to be in Tampa Sunday. Oh yea, all of you AFC fans ere thinking that New England would rise again. And those New Yorkers thought that the Giants would represent the NFC and return to the most luxurious Sunday of the year. And some of you thought that Tony Dungy would re-take his Colts, before he retired with his best-selling book proceeds. Well, we were all wrong and we now have (Mike) Tomlin and the Steelers versus Kurt Warner and the Cardinals. And the only thing they have in common is that neither was supposed to be in Super Bowl 43. Pittsburgh, under its black, second-year coach, has come to be known for its awesome defense. And according to Cleaver, Ike, Carl, and Lloyd, Pittsburgh will slaughter Arizona. But, some of us will remember Kurt Warner, who conducted the “Greatest Show On Turf”. He was the pass-happy quarterback under the (Dick) Vermeil-led St. Louis Rams (who went on to the Super Bowl). So it will an “Arm and Hammer” game that will keep us glued to our big screens, at least until the multi-million-dollar commercials begin. Laugh of the Day: Chiefs will be in Super Bowl 44, after going undefeated in 2009. And Carl Peterson will be the General Manager of the opposing NFC team and guess who will be the Head Coach?.. Ha Ha Ha! Charles Allen: Pittsburgh by 14. Experience, experience, experience! Paul Booker: Pittsburgh by 14. I’m black and biased...Tomlin goes all the way! Carl Clark: Pittsburgh by 7. Defense will win this game! Bubba Cleaver: Pittsburgh by 14. Arizona is the biggest fluke in NFL history! Ike Gardner: Pittsburgh by 7. Too much defense! Lloyd Greenfield: Pittsburgh by 7. Steelers will steal it! Ollie Hubbard: Pittsburgh by 7. Ain’t no mountain high enough! Ed West: Pittsburgh by 10. Remember, I went to Pittsburgh. Tracy Allen: Pittsburgh by 7. Steeler’s “steel” will contain Fitzgerald, Warner Eric Wesson: Pittsburgh by 17. It is a great time to be black in America! Donna Stewart (publisher): Arizona by 7.

LLOYD GREENFIELD I was a firefighter in this community for over 30 years. I have seen men and women perform under the worst of disasters. Thus, knowing about courage and skill is something I have come to expect from every professional, especially those in such high-paid, visible sports professions. Which brings me to my commentary about our sinking Kansas City Chiefs. Something is definitely wrong with our team, y’all! Maybe it’s the management who seems to say it is “my way or the highway”. Or maybe it is the offensive line, who continually allow the quarterback and running backs no opportunity at all. I know for sure that the top management is the “weakest link”. As a firefighter, the chiefs always encouraged, inspired, and supported all of us who were on the frontline. Not a day went by when we knew we were on the “same team”. But that is not happening with our Chiefs and the result is a winless season for the Chiefs, joining St. Louis , Tennessee , and Tampa Bay . But after seeing the game against Dallas , there is some hope, especially among the defensive players. While I haven’t given up, I do believe they will lose again on Sunday against Washington. Carl Clark, More Opinions And The Chiefs Carl Clark was in the Navy and travelled extensively. That introduction to the world has netted him many friends and benefits. In fact, he earned the nickname “Sweet Pea” because he is generally a likeable guy. Because of that, he is well known across the metropolitan area, especially in social circles. He is the “grand-master of the 6902 Club” and has served as president of the prestigious Ivanhoe Club. But, his real passion is the safety of children. You can see him any day at Fifty First and Main, caring for the children who have to cross the street to Visitation Catholic school. For doing such a good job and being well-liked, he is known as the “priest of safety”. Since 1995, he has been there on that corner, doing what he feels is his calling....protecting the kids from predators and crazy drivers. But, Carl is best known for his role in the Monday Niters, He is so opinionated that his fellow friends are noting that he is getting more like that Ike Gardner, everyday. Carl, who used to support the Chiefs is now voting against them, week after week. In fact, he said the Chiefs will not win more than five games this season. To his chagrin,the Chiefs have already won four and are looking any day for that fifth victory. .So at his house Monday night, everyone was kidding Carl about the above picture....that shows him holding up the number “five”. Like other doubters, Carl is having to rethink his early predictions and yet he holds to his prediction and says the Chiefs will lose to Tennessee Titans by a field goal.. Except for Ike, his fellow Monday Niters disagree. Let’s now look in and see what the rest of the guys think. Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still concerned about this Alzheimer’s disease. Particularly, he is warning all care-givers that it takes more than “24-7” to look after those, with Alzheimer’s. But he is quite optimistic about the Chiefs, especially the coaching aspect. Thus, he sees Sunday as another victory for Kansas City. Chiefs by 7. PAUL BOOKER: Interested in all the violence, Booker has high praise for Jackson County. The County has just released a plan to curtail some of the violence and he is elated about that. And he’s happy about the Chiefs being 4-0. He says it is strictly because of those linebackers....Hali, Houston and Johnson. Chiefs by 10 Bubba Cleaver: He is up to his neck in dealing with the government “shutdown” in Washington. He attends every session, hoping for a resolution. . . but there is definitely a war going on in the nation’s capital.. But Cleaver is keeping the faith and still earning national respect, every day. Just like the Chiefs. No doubt about Sunday. Chiefs by 7. Ike “Out of Control” Gardner: Ike is intelligent, committed but cantankerous as hell. He flatout disagrees with everybody, except his current and past St. James pastors, both Rev. and E-3. He did say a few nice things about Dontari Poe, the Chiefs defensive nose guard. But, he was Ol’ Ike when it came to the outcome, Tennessee by 3. Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd, unlike painful Ike, is a mild-mannered, thoughtful guy. He feels that educated people are more effective, when they share their talents with lesser educated people. This “team” approach will make the city, better for everyone. Further, he is pleased with the Chiefs’ team play and Jamaal Charles in particular. They will shine again in Tennessee Sunday. Chiefs by 7 Ollie Hubbard: Big Hub is one of Lincoln University’s greatest advocates. If Lincoln is having a fundraiser, Ollie will call you at 3 a.m., to remind you of your “forced” promise to buy a ticket to a Lincoln event. That dedication has earned him many friends. Just like his wisdom in supporting the Chiefs, this Sunday. Chiefs by 7 Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly: He is really gung-ho about this mental health and violence stuff. His family is running from him because he is urging them to get involved in this community issue. His grandson, Christian, says his grandfather is all about “liberating mental health”. In fact, he notes a mental uplift in the Chiefs. The special teams are leading the way., including this Sunday. Chiefs by 7 Ed West: He keeps wondering why local control of the police department keeps coming up. With people leading the board like Alvin Brooks, Ed asks “what’s the problem”? Chiefs by 3 Congressman Bubba Cleaver: man of the cloth, he is so thankful to have a “fabulous” family and an “unusally high” number of friends and supporters, And he says the Chiefs should thank God for the best, complementary running-back duo in the NFL...Charles and Jones. And while still mad at the Chiefs for now over 40 years, he says they should be thankful for two-time, All-Pro, Brian Waters. Seattle by 10 Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd is thankful for “life”, in general. Certainly he includes his family and his many friends in that statement. Chiefs by 7 Ollie Hubbard: You remember last week, Ollie went on and on about his “earth angel” wife, Sandra. And it wasn’t even Thanksgiving. But, this week he is adding to his list his two “classy” daughters and his brilliant granddaughter, Karrington. Plus, the many who depend on him for local and national news. And like Lloyd, he, too, feels Bowe has arrived and just might make All-Pro, Especially if the Chiefs luck up and win the West. . . Keep being thankful, Ollie. Chiefs by 3 Jim Nunnelly: Feels that the Chiefs defense, led by Tamba Hali, is grossly over-looked. Hali is only second to Derrick Thomas and Neil Smith, when it comes to forcing fumbles. And yes, look for the fifth year linebacker to be All-Pro this year. Personally, Grand Dad is thankful for his wife, two adult children and the five grandchildren (who have made major career decisions this year). And he also is thankful for the Call, the Carter Broadcast Group and Swope Health Services for standing behind the teenagers in our city. And he looks for Hali and the Rockets to stop Seattle cold. Chiefs by 14 Ed West: Wouldn’t you know that this computer genius would make his wife and family, along with his health, as his most-thankful-for part of his life? That’s well-rounded Ed. Ed says the Chiefs were just lucky to have landed a defensive leader who has been to the Super Bowl five times, in various capacities. Monday Night Football For the most part, we again ignored the awful plight of the Kansas City Chiefs, this past Monday. We were entertained at Ike’s house, out in Raytown. Look at that offensive line who has helped Charles and Jones become All-Pro prospects. He’s been voting for the Chiefs all year long, despite voting against them all last year. But Paul is more supportive this year. Always a Chiefs’ supporter ever since he came to town, way back in 1966. A veteran of the Air Force and a graduate of Lincoln university, Paul is a very likeable educator, having taught at Woodland, Switzer, Southeast Middle, Greenwood and C.A. Franklin schools. Monday Niters Marvin Gaye, VIPs, And The Chiefs Marvin Gaye is best known for his smash hit song, “Let’s Get It On”. But my favorite, Marvin Gaye song is “Inner City Blues”. In this seventies song, Marvin highlights what it’s like to be an outsider and a non-participant in the American dream. In fact, at one point in the song he screams. . . “makes me want to holler and throw up both my hands”. Well, given the last few seasons, the Chiefs have sure made a lot of fans “holler and throw up both hands. But, there is a new sheriff and deputies in town and let’s just wait and see what if we can lower our collective hands. Okay, it was important for me to say that first. Speaking of importance, the Monday Niters were special guests of the Kansas City Chiefs this past Tuesday. Yes, the Chiefs treated us like we were royalty up at their training camp in St. Joseph. They gave us special parking passes, covered and cool sideline seating, lots of beverages, and a ton of material. . . all to emphasize that the 2012 Chiefs are no longer alive. They are dead. And in their place are notables like a new quarterback, Alex Smith and a first-picked, first-round offensive lineman named Eric Fisher. The new coach, Andy Reid, walked around the field like he had “star-trek” hope for these new, improved Chiefs. Joining from the past are the exciting Jamaal Charles, at running back and Dwayne Bowe, acrobatic receiver. This mix of old and new will get its first opportunity-to-impress tonight, against the New Orleans Saints, in a doesn’t-count, preseason game. But it does count for the Chiefs. If the Chiefs should lose, the fans will “holler” louder than before. And the renewed promise of a “new day” will slipper into the usual “hang-ups, let-downs, bad breaks, and set-backs”. And of course, there will be a designated player, appointed to tell the fans why we should believe that the Chiefs still deserve our support and that they “will” be better than last year’s 2-14 record. But, oh if they win! The “holler” will be converted into “screaming for joy”. The hang-ups will be reduced. The let-downs will be lifted up. The bad breaks will be forgiven. And the set-backs will be forgotten. And we will look forward to the regular season, with “red colors” draped all over us. But, like a line in Marvin Gaye’s song says, “only God knows where the Chiefs are headed”. We sure don’t. First Lady Mila Lewis Banks, Unchanging Things And The Chiefs Mila Banks threw her own 100th birthday party, over at the Marriott at 45th and Main last Sunday. About 400 former students, fellow educators, and Christian friends stood in line to congratulate such a remarkable woman. And at the dinner party, we, Monday Niters and wives attended and, were represented by cantankerous Ike Gardner. It was Ike’s idea to make “Ms. Banks” an honorary Monday Niter. That’s because she is a loyal reader and a good friend to so many of us. So, Ike presented her with a trophy and told that crowd that she will be making her Chiefs’ predictions, right along side ours. But last Monday night Gen Greenfield prepared a dinner of fresh sweet potatoes and freshly fried fish and a phenomenal salad. Who could argue about anything, with a meal like that in front of you? So the Monday Niters, along with the Go-Along group spent the entire night, talking about how African Americans have been failed by various educational ploys. Here is how some of the conversation went. After that, we will give our predictions on the Buffalo-Chiefs game, coming up Sunday in Buffalo. Ms. Banks will make her prediction, as well. Here goes: There was a time in Kansas City’s history when students coming from the Deep South were routinely put back a grade. Also, during segregation days, black children from Independence, Excelsior Springs and Pleasant Hill were bussed into the Kansas City Mo., School District. Well into the sixties, there were still one-room schools in the state of Georgia. In the Bootheel of Southeast Missouri, black students were bussed up to 60 miles each day to attend school. Because cotton was “king”, black kids went to school in “split sessions” i.e. their school year was interrupted to allow for the picking and chopping of cotton. Ms. Banks attended school in Mount Vernon, about 46 miles west of Springfield, Mo. Because of its erudite faculty, Lincoln High school was rated highly nationwide. Earning college credit while in high school is not a new thing. This was done in the sixties through such great educators like Jeremiah Cameron, Neal Herrford and Chester Anderson. Dr. Charles Allen attended Sumner Elementary and Ike, Carl and Lloyd attended, Wendell Phillips way back in the thirties and forties. Ed West attended school in Osawatomie, Kansas and Jim Nunnelly attended segregated schools in Columbia, Mo. Ms. Banks received unexpected help with her tuition to Lincoln university, way back in the thirties. Today, educating black kids is still an issue in Kansas City.Students who want to leave the unaccredited Kansas City, Mo., School District to attend a nearby accredited school district, are met with the problem of who is to pay for all of this.....the more things change, the more they stay the same. Brandon Lloyd, Alicia Keys, And The Chiefs Did you hear about the butt-kicking New England handed the league-leading Houston Texans, last Monday night. We gathered over to Ed West’s, to watch what we thought would be a good game. It didn’t happen. The Brady Bunch slaughtered the Texans, 42-14, with Brady tossing four touchdown passes. On the bright spot is that game was Kansas City’s own, Brandon Lloyd. We remember Brandon’s high school days out at Blue Springs. From there, he went on to star at wide receiver, at the University of Illinois. And then, he has caught passes for the Denver Broncos, the St. Louis Rams and now the New England Patriots. Known for his acrobatic catches, this guy is “on fire”. It is not every receiver who has the best passer in NFL history as his passing mate. Look for more. Speaking of being “on fire”. Have you heard Alicia Keys’ latest CD, “This Girl Is On Fire”. It is selling like wildfire. If you have seen the video, she paints the story of a young woman, taking on the struggles and joys of life. Not to be outdone, she has to be “on fire”, just to make it. This song has rapidly become the spokes-song for millions of young women, adrift in this world. But, to me, her CD begs the question. . . who is NOT “on fire”. You guessed it. It’s the Kansas City Chiefs. Two buckets of gasoline and a box of matches won’t light up the Chiefs, these days. They have been down so long that “getting up” don’t even cross their minds. With only two wins again eleven losses, the network commentators don’t even comment on the score, demonstrating their neglect of and disdain for these Chiefs. In fact, talking about the Chiefs was so dull. . . that we found ourselves talking about Robert Griffin III. . . the old time Georgy Burger. . . how integration killed the economic spirit of 18th and 12th streets. . . Tom Brady’s record of a passing touchdown for forty two consecutive games. . . Charles Kynard, premier organist who played at the Blue Room in the sixties...how the post office, the school district and the automotive industry were the plum jobs of the ‘50s, ‘60s, and ‘70s. . . how Carl Clark ignored the state-line boundaries and found Mary Lynn in Kansas City, Kas. Actually, our discussion had more “fire” than the Chiefs have. In fact, our discussion soon landed into a healthy respect of years-gone-by. When we were all in one neighborhood and acted and thought unity. When our business owners were our neighbors and our churches were our uniform resource. Yes, when the Chiefs could walk on water, while being “on fire” at the same time. When being from Kansas City was something to behold. . . not to silently mention, in passing. Where did it all go? We don’t know but we wish we had those same pride-filled moments back. And it won’t get any better out in Oakland, this coming Sunday. The Monday Niters have given up on the Chiefs and all that they stand/stood for. Bottom line, the “fire next time” is a long time away. Charles Allen: I’m holding on. Raiders by 13 Lloyd Greenfield: Chiefs are a broken vessel. Raiders by 14 Ollie Hubbard: I’m praying at Ebenezer. Toss-up Jim Nunnelly: Fire is out for Romeo. Raiders by 7 Ed West: No Bowe, no go! Roberta Flack And Monday Niters: ‘Killing Me Softly’ Y’all remember Roberta Flack. She was quite the talk, back in the ‘60s and ‘70s. Her hit song, “Killing Me Softly”, found its way into all of our hearts and homes. But she sang another song, which is so appropriate for our “sinking fast” Chiefs. That song will be revealed after we talk a little about the New Orleans Saints, the Chiefs’ next opponent on Sunday. First of all, the Saints came into being as an NFL expansion team, back in the late ‘60s. Their rise to Super Bowl status has been phenomenal, especially since they had a rough, rough start. Some insensitive sportswriters once called them the “Aints”, owing to their winlessness. Now years later, we all have forgotten about those lean days and nowadays, always look to the Saints to be a contender to win the NFC South Division. Routinely now, they always play well against Division opponents like Atlanta, Carolina and Tampa Bay. But as of today, the Saints have not won a game, so far, this season. Some say it is the atmosphere. Recently, the Saints found themselves deep in controversy after the well-publicized bounty scheme. That fiasco left them without their head coach, Sean Payton, for all of this season. That penalty may well explain why the Saints are off to a rough start. But, what about the Chiefs? What can they say to explain another “shaky” beginning? What can the Chiefs do to make it all better? Actually, we, Monday Niters, believe the Saints will recover soon and start making championship plans. But not so for the Chiefs. Why is that so, you may ask. Well, this is where we talk again about Roberta Flack. Her “other” hit song was “The Closer I Get To You”. In that song, she is happy with the progress of her rising relationship. In fact, she proudly comments that her lover makes her “see” things more clearly. Well, the “closer” we get to the Chiefs, the more we “see” how inept, how inadequate these bunch of bums are. Starting with the coaches, the front office and their regrettable quarterback, Matt Cassel. You don’t have to “get close” to see that these Chiefs are never gonna rise up. They are never gonna win our division again. They can stay here another 50 years and it will all be same. Full of excuses. Full of explanations. And full of crap. And crap it is, no matter how close you get. In fact, we should start referring to them as the “Aints”. Because they aint gonna never be nothing. So for Sunday’s game, it will be the Saints vs. the new Aints. And you don’t have to be “close” to predict the outcome. Roberta Flack would sang another song about the Chiefs. The farther I get from you, the better I seem to be. Monday Niters, what say you? Peanute Brittle, Melody Lanes And The Chiefs We, Monday Niters, have given up on the Chiefs. They have been beaten badly by the doormats of the NFL, i.e. Buffalo and Detroit. What’s more they have lost their only offensive hope through injury. . .Jamal Charles. All they have left now is Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel. Yes, that’s an appropriate name for Cassel because he is worth only “peanuts” and he is always injured, therefore, “brittle”. So, he is now a bona fide member of a long line of “broken” Chiefs’ quarterbacks. So, we collectively think the Chiefs will get shocked again Sunday by the San Diego Chargers. The Chargers will strike the Chiefs for with six or seven touchdowns. Speaking of strikes, we talked a lot about old bowling alleys and good bowling athletes. There have been several bowling establishments frequented by African Americans in the ‘60s -- Monarch Lanes, Melody Lanes, King Louie East and even K.C. Bowl in Kansas. And of late, there is a major bowling contingency that now goes to Premier out in Raytown. Just go out there on a Tuesday afternoon and see scores of seniors rolling the ball. And on Fridays and Thursdays, you can find some of the best bowling around. So, in this column, we prefer to talk about bowlers of yesteryears, rather than talk about Peanut Brittle And The Candy Stripers. So now for a walk down Memory Lanes. Dr. Charles Allen: Way back in 1952, Doc was a pin-setter at Sakin’s bowling alley, near Linwood and Troost. In the old days, bowling pins were set manually, and usually by African American youth at white establishments. Though he did not bowl much, he felt unsafe in that job. But not unsafe about the locals. Chiefs by 3 Paul “6902” Booker: Booker believes the there is no way that the Chiefs can beat San Diego. And he has felt that way since he came here in 1966. He does remember Fred Broski’s bowling for dollars. Money or not. San Diego by 40 Carl “Classy” Clark: Believes the Chiefs are just pitiful. But does remember being a league bowler at Melody Lanes in 1965, on a team sponsored by Northwestern Mutual Insurance Company. Not enough insurance for the Chiefs to win, though. San Diego by 14 Congressman “Bubba” Cleaver: Believes the Chiefs are “out of and out for the season. Wisely, Cleaver has appointed a group to research and honor the black bowlers of the past. This group includes Jauqua Preston, Joe Newsome, Nero Hartridge, Ron Winfrey, Maxine Walker, LaDonna Hendrix, Sam Coleman, Jiles Dunn, Deborah Cheadle Thomas, Joycelyn Burgo, Alex Harris, Willie Henderson Jim Nunnelly and Bill Johnson. An announcement is expected soon on the outcomes. Outcome bad for Chiefs. San Diego by 10 Ike “Spoiled by Niecie’s” Gardner: Ike was pin-setter at a white bowling alley in the ‘50s. As a worker, he had to use the back door to enter. Now, that was a long time ago. He hated segregation as much as he hates the Chiefs. San Diego by 35 Lloyd “Loyal Up To A Point” Greenfield: Lloyd is one of the seniors who bowl at Premier on Tuesdays. Bowling a cool 152 average, he is surrounded by seniors who can really bowl and who know a lot about Kansas City’s history. But, this time, Lloyd switches over from the Chiefs. San Diego by 7 Ollie “Breaking New ” Hubbard: Ollie remembers going to parties at the Rhythm Lanes on Troost, way back in the sixties. The teenagers went there for music and refreshments. But, the Chiefs are not refreshing at all and he expects a bolt of lightning to hit the Chiefs. San Diego by 35 Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: started bowling at King Louie East, when Ron Winfrey became the first black to manage a bowling establishment. Hopes to record some of this rich bowling history. But history will be made Sunday when the Charges run up the largest score in NFL history on the Chiefs. San Diego by 50 Ed “Still Mentoring” West: Being brought up in Osawatamie, Kansas, Ed was only permitted to bowl one night a week at the white bowling alley. However, later he joined the St. James bowling league in 1980. Never a true bowler, he feels the Chiefs have no coach, no offense, no defense thus no win. San Diego by 38

Romeo’s Leadership, Community, And The Chiefs This past Monday night, we talked a whole lot. A lot went down this week. Especially with the Chiefs’ victory and the murder-suicide tragedy piercing the nation’s headlines. But, before we get to that, we had some community-minded guests to join us. One was Tony G from Hot 103 and the others were the Go-Along Club and Andre Jackmon, a supervisor in the Behavioral Health department at Swope Health Services. Thus, we want to tell you a little about them and then comment on Romeo’s leadership, through a double-crisis week with his team. • TONY G. . . for 19years, this young man has led the Toy and Food Drive for all of Kansas City. For this effort, he has been awarded boundless recognition but he still presents as eager as if it’s the very first time. Many don’t know but Tony G was a credible basketball player in the old Catholic leagues. Moreover, his name carried forwarded to the radio airways and he is featured each morning in “drive time”, delivering a morning start for thousands of metropolitan residents. He has also assisted in the development of the popular teen talk show, Generation Rap on Hot 103. But for Tony, this annual food event is just being a good neighbor. Having grown up near 39th and Prospect, Tony G just gives back to his community. In fact, he demonstrates his commitment year after year, making sure that families have food and kids have toys for Christmas. Big kudos for Tony G. • THE GO ALONG CLUB. . . This is group of middle-aged men who get together frequently. However, social-minded the group may appear, they raise thousands of dollars each year for college scholarships. They too were on-hand to talk about their community service, especially providing worthy students with money to go to college....raised through their own corporate resources. We cannot say enough about the men who help our community...each and every day. • ANDRE JACKSON, SWOPE HEALTH SERVICES. . . starting out as just a worker, Andre is now a supervisor in the Behavioral Health department. Andre is involved in establishing counseling and case management services, in and around schools. So far, he has mobilized many agencies and most important, helped his agency get services to those who need it. Andre is one of the rising young men in our community who defy the inappropriate stereotype of young black men. Andre called on us Monday Niters and the others to assist our children, even if just saying an encouraging word. He reiterated that our young people want and need our help. Well, what a night for Monday Niters. . . to hear and see our men, stepping up to help out in their community. Also, there was a lot of conversation about the Chiefs. Mainly, about Romeo and how he handled a team, wrought with confusion caused by the suicide of one of the their fellow players. One that also included a murder of the player’s girlfriend. And one that required getting that team ready to play a game, the next day. So, we took a poll among our members and guests and commented on Romeo Crennel’s finest moment in his profession. On Sunday, Romeo will take his team back to his former place of employment, Cleveland. Where he once coached the Browns and now will return a national hero. Here’s what we think: Dr. Charles Allen: Romeo was quite admirable this week. Chiefs by 7 Paul Booker: He was outstanding handling all that pressure. Browns by 10 Carl Clark: He did a good job but he didn’t save his. Browns by 10 Ike Gardner: He held it together. Because of that, I will pay his bus fare to his next job. Browns by 3 Lloyd Greenfield: He handled the situation, using family values. Browns by 3 Jim Nunnelly: God must love Romeo. Chiefs by 7 Ed West: His demeanor saved the Chiefs....and his job. Chiefs by 3 Joe Webster: Romeo earned himself one more year. Chiefs by 3 Andre Jackmon: Romeo handled the media well...go Raiders no prediction Hadley Reimal: Admirable job under difficult circumstances. Chiefs by 3 Ron Walton: Return to Cleveland will return him to reality. Browns by 10 Sanders Martin: Romeo should be back next year. Monday Niters To Be Featured Before Chiefs’ Game with pic By The Sports Guy Some of the members of the infamous Monday Niters, who have been watching Monday Night football together for 34- years, will be featured on the Tailgate show Monday night on Channel 9 before the Chiefs play or get beat by the Tennessee Titans. The group has a column that has been featured in THE CALL with their football predictions of Chiefs’ games since 1980 but began with their New Year’s column in 1970. They rotate around to each members home for dinner on Monday nights. The Sports Guy has had the opportunity to attend a couple of Monday night games at the home of Jim Nunnelly and recently Ed West. They are all really a great group of guys. There is a great deal of wisdom and history in the room and they will even be helping The Sports Guy pass out Christmas baskets to needy families next week, but have to tell you. If you really want to watch a football game and actually hear what is said, don’t go near them on Monday night, you won’t hear a thing. Anything that you can think of is a topic of discussion. Ike Gardner boasts that he has won the most games overall in the group’s history of course he is immediately challenged by Lloyd Greenfield, Carl Clark and Paul Booker even wakes up to challenge Gardner’s claim that he has won the most games. “I want to tell you all something. I am not opposed to the Chiefs as much as some of you all are. You paint the picture that I am always against the Chiefs. I am only against them when they are playing a team that they cannot beat. I have never said that they Chiefs are going to lose all of the time,” said Gardner. “See that ole’ fat mouth Nunnelly started that,” Gardner yelled. Of course Nunnelly denies doing any such thing. Ed West shares the secret of the groups long term success. “Our wives deserve most of the credit. They cook for all of us and make their homes presentable for guests. They are very gracious hosts for a bunch of ragga’ muffins,” said West. “It is a lot cheaper now to host a game than it was when I first joined the group 25-years ago. Nobody drinks anymore so we don’t have the cost of buying alcohol,” West said. There are countless photos of the group through the years and the events that they have attended both in Kansas City and St. Louis when there was a group of Monday Niters there. And there were too many New year’s parties to count. There is even a Governor’s Cup trophy that the group competed against St. Louis with.

Nat ‘King’ Cole, The Christmas Song, And The 10-3 Chiefs For those of you under 50, you probably missed a treat, not hearing all the songs ever recorded by Nat “King”Cole. Every year about this time, that smooth, velvety voice makes its way into our ears, hearts, and mind. And for us over fifty, we recall that Ol’ King Cole was the very first African American to host his own tv show. Now, that’s something. Belting out songs like, “You Send Me” and of course, no one can forget, “Unforgettable”. But, the song that keeps on giving and selling is “The Christmas Song”. Now you may like Mary J. Blige and Johnny Mathis and even Donnie Hathaway. But none can top Ol’ King Cole when it comes to validating the coming of Christmas. Now for us in Kansas City, we are splitting our time between getting ready for Christmas and getting our Chiefs ready for the playoffs. Baltimore and Miami are like us, waiting for the final word that they are “in the running for the February Super Bowl”. But teams places like Oakland and Tennessee and even Atlanta are singing along, with Nat King Cole and his perennial, “Christmas Song”. That’s all they can sing about, through now. So for us, the song ought to be a reminder that the 10-3 Chiefs are back and have recovered from a dismal last year. Most important, we have proved that Booker and Cantankerous Ike Gardner wrong. They said the Chiefs would not win more than five games this and already they have doubled that. So, I wish they could create a Christmas Song that would memorialize those kind of doubters. Perhaps we could call it, “Wrong Way Ike” and, “Poor, Pitiful Paul”. But thank God for the rest who have/had faith in the Kansas City Chiefs. They can now say proudly that “yes, there is a Santa Claus” and croon along with Nat “King” Cole, at the same time. It’s beginning to look a lot like Christmas. Let’s hear from the rest of the guys. Shakespeare, Some Common Quotes, And The Chiefs When the Chiefs are losing, we search hard for something to talk about. And since the Chiefs have won just one game, we found ourselves talking about something odd. . . William Shakespeare, the best known playwright in the English language. Now, this genius wrote thirty eight plays and many poems, as far back as five hundred years ago. Besides the Bible, his works are quoted more than any other form of literature. His most notable plays include Macbeth, Othello, Richard III, and Midsummer Night’s Dream. And Shakespeare was quite versatile. . . having wrote comedies, histories, character studies and a lot about politics. What would Shakespeare have said about the Chiefs? We will find out, after looking closer at Sunday’s game against the barely-alive Oakland Raiders. First, a little about Oakland. Like the Chiefs, the Raiders were part of the old American Football League, starting way back in 1960. Right away, the Chiefs and the Raiders became rivals, playing some real close games both at Municipal Stadium and the “Black Hole”. The Hubbards, Opinions, And The Chiefs The Monday Niters are full of themselves. They freely share their opinions and don’t care if anyone agrees with them or not. As usual, there was a feast. African cabbage, red beans and rice, chicken wings, catfish, spaghetti, green beans and potatoes, cole slaw, cornbread and rolls. Even their lovely daughter, Kim, dropped by to taste the Hubbard Buffet, But, there was something different tis week. Usually, Ollie does all the cooking. But this time, it was his sassy wife, Sandra, who did it all. Yes, Sandra. Now, she is no stranger to the culinary arts. Her late mother was truly a great cook. In fact, in Macon, Missouri, Mrs. McElroy was a well-known caterer throughout north central Missouri. Now, if you don’t know where Macon is. It near Clarence, Missouri. Don’t know where that is. It’s near LaPlata, Still don’t know? Forget it. Neither do most people. But Sandra was the only black child in the school band. And she was the first black child born in the Macon County hospital. And she spent most of her days, living and thriving in an all-white world. But if you tasted her buffet on Monday, one would know she is truly an African American artist, when it comes to cooking. But husband Ollie was present and offered his supervision to the whole process. Bottom line, the Hubbards did their thing, especially on Monday night. . . sharing their cooking talents and opinions. Aaron Alexis, Mental Health Conference, And The Chiefs Just like always, our country is faced with another mental health dilemma, Someone kills up a lot a people and we turn our attention to the crime, and not the events leading up to the horror. Thank God, we are going to have a conference here in Kansas City that will address the entire issue of mental health and mental illness. Yes, this Saturday at the Downtown Marriott, everyday folks will have an opportunity to talk about this woefully overlooked and under-discussed field. In fact, about 50 people from the urban core of Kansas City are signed up to participate in the day-long conversation. It’s all about planning and for once, we will be at the table, before it happens. Now, what does this all have to do with the now-winning Chiefs. Well, mental health controls everything we do. . . everything we think. . . and everything we try to do. And the Chiefs have been in a deep depression, for a long, long time. And now it appears that they are pulling themsellves out of it. That’s just what we all have to do. Address squarely the problem we are facing. The Chiefs went out and got a quarterback, some offensive linemen and a new coach. . . to address the losing streak and loss of fans. And they are gaining the fans back, with their early efforts in the season. Dr. Charles Allen, Paul Booker, Bubba Cleaver, Lloyd Greenfield, Jim Nunnelly, and Ed West predicted that the Chiefs would win against Philadelphia. Of course, that cantankerous Ike Gardner and that garrulous Carl Clark thought the Chiefs have not changed, from last season. But face it, the depression is lifting. The Chiefs are talking and looking better these days. They are working hard at addressing the things that hurt them. Just like we as individuals should do. As we must do from time to time, we must remove cewrtain people from our lives. . .so that we can do better. In fact, the Chiefs are a lesson in regaining their mental health. So, Dr. Allen will be going to the conference on Saturday to talk about Alzheimer’s season. Jim Nunnelly will be addressing the stigma, associated with people who are struggling mentally. And Andrea Buford will be facilitating discussion tables, down at the Marriott. It will all be part of a historical time where we in the urban community, will be talking about the future and not arguing about the past. Maybe the first topic of discussion will be. . . how did the Chiefs overcome their depression. The answer is simple and complex. It took a lot of time, patience, and a lot of support from people who used to love them. All of you are invited to the Marriott on Saturday. Come see how to deal with mental health issues. With you becoming the focal point. . . for your own mental health.

Tribute To A Monday Niter Bunny Rabbit: A True Brother Who Had No Brothers Stewart Watson was a big, giant of a guy, who always wore a smile and had a baritone-like laugh. He was “at home” whereever he went, whether in his favorite club on Prospect or whether meeting you for the first time. He clearly will be missed by all of us Monday Niters for he was one of the founding members of this adult “boys club”. To most of us, he had been friends for all of his 24,582 days on this earth. But on July 3, of this year, “Bunny Rabbit” left this earth and thus, the basic reason for this column. In short, we want to say “good bye” in a way that only friends who have known you a lifetime, can say it. So let’s start with “Bunny Rabbit” and his relentless use of nicknames. “Bunny Rabbit” had a nickname for everyone in our group. That’s because he wanted each of us to know that he liked each of us individually and collectively. Ollie was “Mr. Puddy Pot” and Ike was “Huff”. Booker was “Chocolate Drop”. Dr. Allen was “Pumpkin” and Carl was appropriately called “Mr. Mary Lynn”. And because of my bald head, he started calling me “Mr. Peanut”. I dare say he would have to stop and think of our real names because that was all he called us, every day of his nearly 69 years. We say nearly because he died just three days before his 69th birthday. And there was no denying him access to you. Even though he moved to St. Louis some years ago, he still managed to see everyone at least once a month or just calling them. Speaking of calling, “Bunny Rabbit” was a phone junkie. Night or day, winter or fall, he would call one of us, out of the clear blue sky. It was as if we were his connection to reality or maybe he just wanted to stay close to his friends. Always the same, joy-induced greeting, “ what u doing boy?”. And then, right from there, the word would spread... “Bunny Rabbit” is in town and somehow, unplanned though it may be, there would be a reunion, right then and there. And it seemed he would always time his visit during one of our Monday Nite Footballers meeting and whatever the conversation on the floor, would give way to his one-man, nickname-calling comedy act. “Bunny Rabbit” was a real friend and the kind of brother to everyone, even though he had no biological brothers or sisters. He exuded brotherhood, at its highest level. In addition, “Bunny Rabbit” was a lesson in kindness and consideration. He reminded us that we all must live our lives, merrily and among friends. He demonstrated that by always dropping by and diverting you from your daily worries and strife. Yes, Bunny Rabbit was a spark of life to all of us and his light still shines in our thoughts and in our conversation. Ike says “Bunny Rabbit” always checked on him whether sick or well. And Ollie says that he has great memories of “Bunny” all the way from elementary school through Lincoln university. But, Dr. Charles Allen concluded the stories about “Bunny Rabbit” best. He simply said that “Bunny Rabbit” extended a hand but he always touched our hearts. What else needs to be said but “Good Bye, ‘Bunny Rabbit’. We are all better off by knowing you and we will wear our nicknames proudly, in your honor.”

Interim Superintendent And The Lowly Chiefs The NFL season is finally here. After a threatened strike, a boatload of free agents, and a new set of feet, the Chiefs will open at Arrowhead on Sunday. And you will see folks going to early morning church services, in order to witness the kickoff game to the 2011 season. And like the tornado that hit Joplin and the hurricane Irene that racked the east coast, the Chiefs have a lot of damage to clean up. You know they released All Pro offensive lineman, Brian Waters. And Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel is ailing, as usual. Then, the Chiefs did not win a single pre-season game, this summer. That all adds up to another questionable season ahead, in spite of the fact the Chiefs made the playoffs last year. In many ways, the Chiefs are like the Kansas City, Mo., School District. Every year, they come up with a different reason why any kind of success evades them. In fact, Big Bad John Covington balanced the budget but he did absolutely nothing to improve the test scores. He closed a lot of schools but did not open up any new academic trails. And once again, Booker says it is purely chaotic, down at 1211 McGee. No one knows what to do about it and that’s tragic. As expected each year, the enrollment, the energy and the ebullience decreases. I suggest that at least the Board ought to hire an Associate Superintendent, whose only job is to monitor the academic progress of our children and keep the community updated on the accreditation status. This person should be a resident of Kansas City and have credibility in our community. This over-reliance on itinerant Superintendents is crazy. And we in this community can change that. We really can. All right, enough of that. Let’s return to talking about the Cheaps (I mean Chiefs). Ike Gardner and Paul Booker are back at their old habits again. They can’t see the Chiefs beating anybody this year. After all, the Chiefs play New England, San Diego twice, Pittsburg, Minnesota, Indianapolis, and even Detroit. That’s what happens when a non-playoff-calibre teams make the playoffs, They suffer greatly the next year. But Carl Clark, Ollie Hubbard, and of course, Dr. Charles Allen believe the Chiefs will be “up” for the challenge and will win their first game, against Buffalo. So, like the School District, the Chiefs are steadily losing their support....both here and nationally. What will it take to get it back for both of these also-rans? It’s simple. Just do SOMETHING right. Anything. Is help on the way? As is our duty, we will monitor the progress and report to you each week. Just like we have been doing for forty two years now. Whew! Time passes, doesn’t it. Hint to the District and the Chiefs.

Kansas City Chiefs vs. Denver Broncos 7:00 p.m. NFL Network Chatter, Commentary and Conversation What does Jesse Jackson have to do with last Sunday’s Oakland-Kansas City game? I’ll answer that after I assess the Chiefs, now just over the half-way point in the season. First, the Chiefs survived. Now, let’s face it, y’all. A win is a win, no matter how ugly. And Sunday’s win against Oakland was not pretty, except for the first and last Kansas City drives. The in-between was horrible, even though it was Trent’s first day back. However, I must say that we could not have done it without Trent. Ed West flat-out confirms that. Further, He feels that Trent’s presence won the game, only because Huard could not have shepherded that last drive. And we all agree that Sunday was the appropriate time to re-insert Trent, even though Huard had done a respectable job. Now,tomorrow will be Trent’s real test. He and Kennison will have to be “connected at the hip”, for the Chiefs to have half a chance. If we should happen to beat Denver, that will put us in good shape for a playoff spot. We know that Denver is vulnerable because San Diego beat Denver and we beat San Diego. In fact, last Sunday, LaDainian ran like crazy. . . just like Jesse did in 1988. Speaking of Jesse Jackson, he really did have something to do with Sunday’s game. But before I tell you, let me reminisce for a minute. Back in 1988, I received a call at the (Samuel) Rodgers Health Center. It was from Fuzzy Thompson, wanting a place to have a rally that featured Jesse Jackson and some farmers from Chillicothe. I agreed but Fuzzy was unsure if it would take place. . .so I kept it a secret from our staff. . .mainly because I did not want to face it, if Jesse failed to come. Well, Jesse did come and so did all those farmers who were about to lose their family farms. Tractors, limousines, and a string of cars paraded right down in the middle of the Wayne Miner projects. And people came from everywhere, to hear and see ol’ Jesse. And when he donned the back door, he immediately started planning who would talk, when, and at what point he would enter. Details. Details. Right there on the spot. I immediately saw how Jesse operated. . .great organizing skills, clear instructions, which included a tribute to Dr. Rodgers and a “thank you” to me for helping out. All within a ten-minute planning session. Jesse stood tall in my books and one could see why he is important to all of us, especially us sports fans. On the way out, I mentioned to Jesse that there were no black head coaches in the National Football League. Jesse, who had been a classy running back at Illinois, told me that he would work on that. A few years later, Jesse started meeting with the owners in the NFL, asking them to include one black coach in the final interviews, only when head coaching vacancies occurred. The owners agreed and today, some 10 years after, there are seven black coaches, proudly running things at various franchises. As of this date, the illustrious field of head coaches now include Lovie Smith Chicago), Marvin Lewis (Cincinnati), Tony Dungy (Indianapolis); Dennis Green (Arizona); and Romeo Cremmel (Cleveland). The remaining two were on the field Sunday, out at Arrowhead. . . Herman Edwards (Kansas City) and Art Shell (Oakland). And that is what Jesse had to do with the game, last Sunday, out at Arrowhead. Thanks, Jesse. You always know what to do and say. Happy Thanksgiving To All Of Our Readers!

Chiefs Have Taken Us Too Far, Too Fast, With Too Little Listening to the Chiefs' front office might lead you to believe that the Chiefs are going to the Super Bowl. Wait a minute. Grant you, the Chiefs are in first place in the Western Division of the American Conference. And yes, they have more wins than losses (4-3). And for you anti-Larry Johnson fans, the venerable Priest Holmes is back (at least for now). And on an even brighter note, Dwayne Bowe is making the Chiefs look good on their first-round draft choice. But, let's get real here. My advice to the Chiefs is "Don't take us too far, too fast, with too little". We are not even half-way through the season and we are shouting, as if the Chiefs have already achieved something. Think about it. In November, the Chiefs still must face Green Bay and Denver at home and the undefeated Colts in Indianapolis. Duh! Now, the shouting should tone down a little. And after our discussion last Monday night, there are great differences among us, as to how the Chiefs will fare, between now and Thanksgiving. Head Hater Ike Gardner and "that" Booker thinks the Chiefs will lose all three of those games. That means that by the time we light up the Plaza, the Chiefs would have slipped to 4-6. But Carl Clark is not going that far. He thinks that the Chiefs will beat Denver and lose to Green Bay and the Colts. And just to give balance to the discussion, Ed West and Lloyd Greenfield think the Chiefs will beat both Green Bay and Denver and lose only to the Colts. They think the Chiefs will be 6-4 by the time we all sit down to Thanksgiving dinner. Now, the question is "who's right". Are the Chiefs taking us "too far, too fast, with too little". As old-time fans, we've been down that yellow-brick road with the Chiefs before. Win a few games and get us all excited and then, in the end, fall slowly to the bottom. But this time, Lloyd and Ed are right on. The Chiefs will win at Arrowhead and lose in Indy. That being said, pass the mashed potatoes, please.

George Jefferson, Fantasies And The 11-5 Chiefs Do you remember “The Jeffersons”? That was a tv show that appeared regularly on CBS, way back in the seventies. This was a Norman Lear production, that attempted to show that black people were “moving on up”. In fact, the show took place in the Jeffersons’ Fifth Avenue apartment, on the upper East Side of New York City. And since the prosperity was all new to the Jeffersons, the writers traced their humorous, everyday activities. Some of it was funny but the whole thing was filled with a lot of fantasy. Speaking of fantasy, the Chiefs have been living on “Fantasy Island”. For the first nine games the Chiefs were the ‘talk of the sports world”. They were undefeated until they met the Payton-laced Denver Broncos. Then the Chargers. Then, the Broncos again. And just like that, the little “fantasy” bubble began to bust. In fact, these same Chiefs lost five of their next seven games, the latest being to the Chargers last Sunday. Talk about up and down. The Chiefs were living in a fantasy world and it all came tumbling down, causing many to mentally eliminate the Chiefs from further contention. But is it over for the Chiefs? Now remember the Chiefs were 2-14 in 2013. And now they are in playoffs and have been there solidly for three weeks running. They didn’t need help from other teams, they clinched a spot and just waited. So, my point is that the “fantasy” continues, in spite of them losing the last third of the season. And last Sunday, they lost but they didn’t use twenty of the first twenty two starters. So, San Diego beat the second and third teamers of the Chiefs. Not Jamaal Charles or Tamba Hali or Derrick Johnson or Dwayne Bowe. So what’s the point? The most salient point is that the Chiefs are still pursuing the NFL Super Bowl game.. Even Carl Clark says let’s support the Chiefs “for the heck of it”. As always, that Paul Booker and Ike Gardner are non-supportive, believing that the Chiefs will lose their first round playoff game to Indianapolis Colts, just like they did a couple of weeks ago.And for sure, that will be “it” for Kansas City and its fantasy season. Hold up for a minute!. The Chiefs did put eight players on the All-Pro roster. And their coach, Andy Reid, will probably be Coach Of The Year. And some second teamers are going to playing a lot, come Sunday afternoon. Thereby, making the Chiefs even better prepared for the upcoming game. Bottom line, like the Jeffersons. . . the Chiefs are “moving on up”. They finally got a piece of the NFL pie. Now Ike will probably predict against the Chiefs. But you all know Ike. He was wrong eleven of sixteen times this year. That means he wasn’t right, most of the time, about the Chiefs. He is not the “Holy Grail” of predicting football games. So, let’s get behind our hometown team and maybe, just maybe….we can “move further on up” to the East side and take on New England and then onto the West side to take on Denver. Wait. Wait. Wait. I’ve drifted back into Fantasy Land. For right now, Chiefs over the Colts. (We hope).
